`camxes.js` and `camxes_postproc.js` are vendored verbatim from [lojban/ilmentufa](https://github.com/lojban/ilmentufa) (MIT-licensed, see `LICENSE` in this directory). `camxes.js` is the PEG.js-compiled parser for `camxes.peg`, the canonical standard Lojban grammar; `camxes_postproc.js` trims/annotates its raw parse trees. They are not modified here.

`glosser/gismu-data.js` is vendored alongside them because `camxes_postproc.js` unconditionally `require()`s it at load time. Only that one file was pulled from the upstream `glosser/` directory — the rest of that directory (jQuery, Bootstrap, images) is upstream's own standalone HTML glosser UI and isn't needed here.

`camxes-exp.js` is vendored verbatim from the same repo, same license. It's the compiled parser for `camxes-exp.pegjs`, "experimental camxes" -- upstream's actively-developed grammar variant, kept in sync with community-proposed vocabulary (lensisku's "experimental cmavo", e.g. `ue'i`) that the canonical `camxes.js` grammar doesn't recognize. It is **not** purely additive vocabulary on top of the standard grammar -- its own changelog documents real syntax changes too (e.g. a brivla/cmevla merge that reclassifies `la` under a different selmaho than standard camxes does). jbolaltci only ever falls back to it when standard parsing has already failed, and flags results that used it (`AnalyzeResult.usedExperimentalGrammar`) -- see `docs/architecture-decisions/003-experimental-cmavo-via-camxes-exp-fallback.md`.
